exercise.name: Glute Bridge Walk

reference.title: Glute Bridge Walk (male)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip extension hold; knees straighten as the feet walk out)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you lift into the bridge, breathe steadily while the heels walk out and back, inhale as you lower.

prescription.progression: Further walk-out, then single-leg bridge, then Nordic or slider curls

cues.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip width, arms by your sides.
Breathe out and lift into a bridge: knees, hips and shoulders in one line.
Keep the hips up and take small heel steps away from you, right then left.
Hips as high as you can keep them, feeling the hamstrings work.
Step the heels back toward you one at a time.
Breathe in and roll the hips down to the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Hips sinking as the feet walk out
mistakes.fix: Take smaller steps and only go as far as you can keep the hips high.
Brace the abs; lift each foot only a few centimetres.
Shorten the walk-out and build up gradually.
Ribs down, slight posterior pelvic tilt.

kinematics.norm: Hips extend to neutral at the top (straight knee-hip-shoulder line); no extra lumbar arch (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the top is the traditional bridge; more knee bend shifts work away from the hamstrings (Lehecka 2017)

kinematics.setup: Hip joint 8.6 cm above the floor
kinematics.peak: 29.4 cm at the top, 23.1 cm walked out
kinematics.norm: Pelvis lifts until the line is straight (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Feet 50.5 cm from the hip line at the top (feet x)
kinematics.peak: 2 heel steps of 10 cm per foot (feet 70.5 cm); each foot lifts about 3 cm mid-step
kinematics.norm: Feet step away until the knees are only slightly bent; hamstring activity rises as the knees straighten (Lehecka 2017)

kinematics.peak: 0.6 s per step out, 0.5 s hold, 0.6 s per step in, 1.3 s down
kinematics.norm: About 0.6 s per step with the hips held up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #17712, Glute Bridge Walk (male) (movement reference only)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Hamstring cramps are common: stop, lower and stretch, then shorten the walk-out.
Low back discomfort: lower the bridge height.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.

muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Co-target: as the feet walk away the knees straighten and the hamstrings take more of the hip extension (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Co-target: as the feet walk away the knees straighten and the hamstrings take more of the hip extension (Lehecka 2017).
